title: Introduction and overview — Westland Lynx
description: Signature-original re-engineering study: introduction and overview of the Westland Lynx. This is a Signature-original design study, explicitly labeled and never presented as public record. Baseline reference: Twin-engine multirole helicopter; service from 1978; 450+ built by Westland; speed-record holder.. The Westland Lynx is a twin-engine multirole helicopter built by Westland (later AgustaWestland), entering service in 1978. A specially modified Lynx set the world helicopter speed record at 249 mph in 1986 — a record that still stands. Over 450 were built in army, naval, and export versions. Signature improvements explored here: Signature composite primary structures cut empty weight ~12% versus the public baseline; Signature avionics suite with predictive-maintenance health monitoring on every major system. Angle: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
